_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face. The pursuer's target sits 190 wu west of the hill and 40 wu below its bottom edge, so its leg is clear of the hill and it charges straight east. Measured with a 2-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 120, the charge makes contact at tick 159 and drives the router back about 60 wu west, the two fight one unbroken melee, and the router routs at tick 344. While the pursuer is still on it the router is shoved south (to about y 675 by tick 440); once clear it flees north along the hill's west side (x about 935, y 620 at tick 560, 454 at tick 680), every man clear of the hill, and rallies at tick 704 at about (937, 415), inside the clip (it ends at tick 720). The pursuer's facing turns smoothly through the charge, with no snap larger than 20 degrees between 2-tick samples. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill: the router's flight never meets it. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. After the rout the pursuer's own deep column deforms: a 2-tick scan of every sample from tick 330 reads a sustained shape residual of 145.8 wu against a 30 wu threshold (the same scan on the pre-#1739 merge-base reads 42.6 wu; at this head the pursuer swings round towards the south-east around tick 598, which is where its body-to-slot gaps jump). Before the charge came straight in (rout at tick 469), the same scan from the rout read 75.4 wu: the straight charge did not cause the deformation. Because of it the declared checks pin the router's story beats with only sparse post-rout samples (400, 560 and 680, plus the clip's last tick, 720, which the catalog cadence already samples) rather than sampling the gallop densely: an extra sample at tick 710 next to 720 makes the pursuer's deformation read as sustained.
